text: ZERODAY. When a security advisory lands, which files in your code should a human read first?

A C V E drops in a library you depend on. You need two answers. Are we exposed? And where in our code do we look? Scanners answer the first one with a wall of alerts. ZERODAY answers both, on your own machine.

Here is the command line. We give it C V E 2021 23337, a code injection bug in lodash, and a small app. ZERODAY reads the public advisory from O S V and checks the lockfile: lodash 4.17.15 is pinned, so this app is affected, and the fix is to upgrade to 4.17.21.
Then it ranks the files. email dot j s calls the vulnerable template function, so it comes first. cart dot j s only imports lodash, so it comes last. No model, no G P U, under two seconds.
The same engine runs in a local web app. You get the verdict, the version to upgrade to, and every ranked file with its line, the code, and the reason.

But rules only know ten weakness types. Missing authorization, broken authentication, regular expression denial of service: there is nothing to pattern match. That is where Antares comes in. Antares one B is Foundation A I's open security model. It explores a repository with tools, like an analyst, and names the files that matter.

Getting it running is one command. antares up starts vLLM with Antares on a GPU in your own RunPod account. This is the real run: ready in two minutes, about fifty cents an hour, and it deletes itself when the time cap is reached. ZERODAY finds the endpoint on its own after that. No config files.

A real advisory: an authentication bypass in Traefik, C W E 287. Given only the weakness type, the rules engine says not scanned, rather than pretending the code is clean. Antares made 65 tool calls through the repository and ranked basic auth dot go first. That is the exact file the real fix changed. It found it in one of two runs. That is why ZERODAY runs Antares twice and merges the answers by vote.

Or scan a whole repository for anything. On OWASP Juice Shop, Antares picked the eight weakness types that fit the code, the rules checked their ten, all in one minute. Three files were flagged by both, so they go to the top of the list.

Does it hold up? We measured it on 36 real advisories across 12 weakness types, published in the last three months, each checked out just before its fix, and given only the C W E. Rules alone ranked the fixed file first 14 percent of the time. Antares alone, 25 percent. Two Antares runs merged, 36 percent, and 42 percent in the top three. Where rules find nothing at all, Antares still hits one in four. Every number reproduces with one command.
When you are done, antares down deletes the pod. This whole recording session, including the benchmark, cost 53 cents.

What it is not. It localizes; it does not prove exploitability, and it never writes exploits. A one billion parameter model misses often, so every answer is a candidate for a human, with evidence you can verify.
ZERODAY is open source under Apache 2. Find it on GitHub at pandeyaby slash ZERODAY. Thanks for watching.
